item.title: Judge rules Trump administration illegally punished AI firm Anthropic
item.description: A judge barred the Trump administration from enforcing a set of rules aimed at cutting off Anthropic from the federal government, ruling the administration had unconstitutionally punished the AI company for protected speech.

item.title: Tropical Storm Dolly forms in the Atlantic Ocean
item.description: Tropical Storm Dolly on Thursday became the fourth named storm in the Atlantic Ocean this year.

item.title: U.S. military uses laser to shoot down 3 cartel drones at southern border, Pentagon says
item.description: The U.S. military this week used a laser to shoot down three drones along the U.S.-Mexico border that were allegedly operated by drug cartels, the Pentagon said.

item.title: LaGuardia air traffic controllers left work early before deadly collision, source says
item.description: Two air traffic controllers at LaGuardia Airport left work early on the night of a deadly runway collision in March, a source familiar with the situation told CBS News.

item.title: Judge temporarily blocks new Postal Service rules for mail voting
item.description: A federal judge on Thursday temporarily blocked the U.S. Postal Service from enforcing its new requirements for mail voting for the November midterm elections.

item.title: Ross Fire burns 85,000 acres, leaves destruction across 2 counties
item.description: The Ross wildfire has burned more than 80,000 acres across Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forcing evacuations, closing roads and disrupting schools.

item.title: More than 1,000 missing, including 65 Americans, as Nepal flood deaths mount
item.description: More than 1,000 people, including many Americans, are still missing along the Nepal-China border after deadly floods and mudflows likely triggered by a glacial collapse.

item.title: DOJ in court to defend Kennedy Center Board's new push to add Trump's name to building
item.description: The Kennedy Center Board, made up of President Trump and his allies, is again fighting to display Mr. Trump's name on the building's facade. CBS News Justice Department reporter Jake Rosen has the latest on Thursday's court hearing.

item.title: Why some jurors in Lindsay Clancy trial won't participate in deliberations
item.description: Jurors began deliberations in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial on Thursday after the prosecution and defense wrapped closing arguments. Boston criminal defense attorney and legal analyst Elyse Hershon joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Marine One's warning calls before mishap went unheard by air traffic controllers
item.description: The NTSB said tower recordings show controllers never heard Marine One's Aug. 4 calls warning it was preparing to take off, though separate recordings confirm the calls were made.

item.title: El-Sayed says he's spoken with Jeremy Moss after Hasan Piker's comments
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee in Michigan's U.S. Senate race, says now is the time for Democrats to work together ahead of the 2026 midterm election.

item.title: What to expect from 2026 NFL season as teams finalize rosters
item.description: Tyler Dragon, an NFL reporter at USA Today, joins "The Daily Report" to break down what to expect from the upcoming football season.

item.title: Netflix shares exclusive extended look at Grand Theft Auto VI
item.description: Netflix is sharing a look at the highly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto VI, set to be released in November. Jordan Minor, a gaming writer at PCMag and author of "Video Game of the Year," joins "The Daily Report."

item.title: Jury to consider lesser charges in Lindsay Clancy trial
item.description: The judge in Lindsay Clancy's trial directed jurors to consider lesser criminal charges in addition to first-degree murder as deliberations began on Thursday. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Key moments from Lindsay Clancy's trial as jury weighs the case
item.description: Lindsay Clancy, 36, has pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder in the deaths of her three children and said she was suffering form postpartum psychosis. A jury is deliberating.

item.title: Golf caddy gets a full ride to University of South Carolina with some help from the club
item.description: The Old Barnwell Golf Club in South Carolina has a special program that focuses on how the club can give back to its caddies. After Daniella Penaloza impressed the club with her work ethic, she received a full ride from the University of South Carolina. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Cyclospora outbreak tied to 3 more states, FDA says
item.description: U.S. officials have confirmed cases of a parasitic illness tied to lettuce in three more states: Georgia, Tennessee and Texas.

item.title: Sailboat theft ends in deadly Rhode Island shootout
item.description: What started with the theft of a luxury sailboat near the foot of Manhattan ended with a deadly police shootout in Rhode Island. Tom Hanson has the details.

item.title: How Dolly Parton used "I Will Always Love You" royalties to support the Black community in Nashville
item.description: Nashville historian David Ewing joins "The Daily Report" to break down how Dolly Parton used her royalties from Whitney Houston's rendition of "I Will Always Love You" to uplift the Black community in the city.

item.title: ICE grants $16.7 million contract to buy thousands of electric shock gloves
item.description: ICE has granted a $16.7 million no-bid contract for 6,000 gloves​ that can deliver electric shocks, a new use-of-force tool that the agency claims will help officers control resisting detainees.

item.title: Republicans, cattle ranchers angry at Trump for beef import tariff suspension
item.description: President Trump visited Texas on Thursday amid criticism of his plans to lower beef prices by importing more beef from overseas. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Closing arguments in trial of man accused in Tupac's murder expected Monday
item.description: Both sides have rested in the murder trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis, who prosecutors allege orchestrated the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur.

item.title: What Trump's renaming of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" means in practice
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order on Thursday to rename Lake Ontario to "Lake America" amid his trade war with Canada. CBS News' Nana-Sentuo Bonsu has more.

item.title: Revisiting one of America's greatest losses in the Revolutionary War
item.description: Thursday marks 250 years since George Washington's Continental Army suffered a brutal defeat at the Battle of Brooklyn. Lindsay Chervinsky, executive director of the George Washington Presidential Library, joins "The Takeout" to discuss how that loss ultimately led to America's triumph in the Revolutionary War.

item.title: Dolly Parton offered to try experimental drugs if "no hope" in her cancer battle
item.description: "She told me recently that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future," Stella Parton said in a Facebook post.

item.title: DeSantis administration misappropriated $10 million in "sophisticated scheme," grand jury says
item.description: $10 million from a Medicaid settlement found its way into a charity tied to the wife of Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis. Despite what a grand jury called a clear misappropriation of funds, no criminal charges are being filed. CBS News Miami investigative reporter Jim DeFede has the details.

item.title: Woman who came to U.S. as child after El Salvador earthquake facing deportation as TPS set to expire
item.description: Recent court orders have paved the way for the Trump administration to end Temporary Protected Status for immigrants from several countries. For people from El Salvador, those protections are set to expire in early September. Daysi Gonzalez, who came to the U.S. as a child and stayed under TPS, joins "The Takeout" to discuss her situation.

item.title: 8/27: CBS Evening News
item.description: Jury deliberating in Lindsay Clancy's trial, Americans among missing in Nepal.

item.title: Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America"
item.description: The executive order directs the Interior Department to update the Geographic Names Information System, changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America.

item.title: 8/27: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Jury deliberations underway in Lindsay Clancy murder trial; President Trump travels to Texas for Ken Paxton Senate fundraiser.
